title: Fugu reframes “model release” as learned orchestration over a model pool
summary: Fugu reframes “model release” as learned orchestration over a model pool : Sakana introduced Fugu , presenting it as a single API that learns model selection, delegation, verification, and synthesis across multiple frontier models; Vercel quickly added Fugu Ultra to AI Gateway. The product thesis resonated with engineers who already see real systems moving toward orchestration layers: @levie called routing/orchestration a likely high-value layer, and @audreyt reported Fugu Ultra working well as a planner/advisor...

title: The critique was immediate: opaque baselines, missing cost accounting, and questionable reporting
summary: The critique was immediate: opaque baselines, missing cost accounting, and questionable reporting : The most detailed teardown came from @eliebakouch , who argues Fugu is essentially a router/classifier plus a preplanned multi-step workflow system, with several core issues: it trails Opus on SWE-Bench Pro by ~10 points , compares against anonymized “Model A/B/C,” omits token/cost reporting for best-of-N style orchestration, and should be compared against other test-time scaling setups rather than plain base mode...

title: Hermes continues to gain surface area as a local/personal agent platform
summary: Hermes continues to gain surface area as a local/personal agent platform : Hermes updates included iMessage access without a Mac , Raft integration as an external agent in a shared workspace , and most significantly GUI control for Windows or Linux desktop apps with any model . The repo also crossed 200K stars , reinforcing that a lot of developer energy is going into agent UX and harness ergonomics , not just base model quality.
